messages:
incident-bot: 🔔 Alert: elevated 5xx and latency for model v5-alpha in us-west1. 5xx rate jumped to ~7.8% over last 3m, P95 latency x3. Signature: kv_cache_miss -> OOM. Auto-created incident thread.

alice_oncall: I'm paged, taking ownership. collecting context now. any customer impact reports?

erin_customer: seeing failures from our sandbox keys, some calls return 500 with 'worker OOM'. A few customers reported degraded chat responses.

ben_sre: I can join. first cut: we should drain traffic from v5-alpha and route to v4-stable fallback to stop OOM cascade. also consider emergency key quotas for heavy keys.

frank_engineer: Agree. v5-alpha rollout had memory-edge change in kv-cache. If it's hitting long prefixes we can OOM GPUs. Rolling back the variant is safest.

carla_product: Who owns the rollout config? We need a fast rollback then postmortem. Also notify account teams for customers currently on canary.

alice_oncall: ben, can you execute traffic swap? frank, can you prepare rollback steps and a short blurb for CS? dave, please draft initial customer note.

ben_sre: Running command now:
```
# move all traffic off v5-alpha to v4-stable in us-west1
redwoodctl traffic update \\--region us-west1 \\--from-model v5-alpha \\--to-model v4-stable \\--weight 1.0
```
I also set per-key soft quota for top 20 heavy keys: 200 rps -> 50 rps to limit blast radius.

deploy-bot: rollback-job 0x7f3a initiated for rollout v5-alpha -> v4-stable. job_id=job-20260315-7f3a.

alice_oncall: copied. frank, what's the safe rollback knob? full deactivate variant or just weight-zero?

frank_engineer: weight-zero is immediate and reversible. deactivating variant deletes cached state; prefer weight-zero + keep variant healthy for diagnostics. Command to zero-weight:
```
redwoodctl variant set-weight \\--model v5-alpha \\--variant canary \\--weight 0.0
```
Will also flip routing policy to prefer v4-stable.

ben_sre: Done. Traffic swap completed at ~+90s. Observability: 5xx rate dropping. P95 latency trending down. Metrics: 5xx -> 0.6% (from 7.8%), P95 down 2.8x.

dave_support: Drafting customer note: "We've observed transient errors affecting some requests routed to a recently rolled out model variant. We've routed traffic back to the stable model and implemented temporary per-key quotas. If you continue to see issues, please reply here or open a ticket." want to tag account teams?

carla_product: Yes tag a1_critical and enterprise-accounts. Add that we're investigating root cause and will share ETA for full rollback/patch.

erin_customer: thanks for the fast response. sandbox looks good so far. We'll escalate if we see anything else.

ben_sre: we also applied a circuit-breaker on the model-level: "max-inflight-per-node=120" to avoid GPU OOM while we investigate. Logs show repeated large-kv-cache allocations from v5-alpha inference path.

alice_oncall: Good containment. For now incident status = mitigated. Next steps: frank to collect heap traces + config diff, ben to run memory-load repro on staging, carla to coordinate customer comms, dave to queue support updates.

frank_engineer: I'll capture trace + stack and open CR with revert candidate. ETA 2h for traces + regression test.

ben_sre: Monitoring window 30m. If no regression, we'll keep v5-alpha weight=0 and treat as pulled. Will run a controlled canary after fix.

deploy-bot: rollback-job job-20260315-7f3a completed successfully. no deployments failed.

alice_oncall: Thanks everyone. I'll mark incident as mitigated in the tracker and will hand off to postmortem owner. If anyone sees reappearance, ping me directly. :white_check_mark:

carla_product: Assign postmortem to frank + ben. Add action item: add automated mem-safety check in rollout pipeline.

dave_support: Customer note posted to accounts channel and GH tickets updated.

ben_sre: Final check: 5xx now steady at 0.2% baseline, P95 normal. Closing active page.

alice_oncall: closing thread; follow-up in #postmortems and internal doc. Thanks all. :pray:
